channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula perde vantagem e empata com Flávio Bolsonaro em eventual 2º turno
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has lost his lead in potential second-round scenarios and is now technically tied with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), according to a Datafolha poll. For the first time, the opponent numerically surpasses the incumbent in voting intentions for a potential 2026 presidential runoff.

item.title: Lula quer incluir devedores do Fies em novo programa de renegociação de dívidas
item.description: President Lula announced that the government plans to include Fies student loan defaulters in a new debt renegotiation program aimed at easing household indebtedness and supporting youth professional training. The initiative, still under development, may be launched in the coming days and is part of a broader package that includes potential use of FGTS funds to settle debts. Lula stressed that regularizing these debts is crucial so students can become qualified professionals and contribute to national development.

item.title: O que se fala nos bastidores sobre a possibilidade de Lula não disputar eleição
item.description: Lula has not yet decided whether to run for re-election in 2026, reflecting a strategic dilemma between his desire to run and the risk of a symbolic defeat to Flávio Bolsonaro, heir to Bolsonarism. Allies indicate his hesitation is not merely rhetorical but a real calculation of electoral cost and the historical impact of a potential loss. The PT’s grassroots mobilization has weakened, making voter decisions increasingly dependent on individual economic perceptions.

item.title: Haddad lança estratégia para enfrentar Tarcísio nos debates e nas urnas
item.description: Fernando Haddad is launching a campaign to challenge Tarcísio de Freitas in the São Paulo gubernatorial race, highlighting his achievements as mayor and minister—such as bike lanes, Prouni, and tax exemptions for those earning up to R$5,000—while attempting to counter criticisms over tax increases during his tenure at the Finance Ministry, particularly the 'tax on small imports,' which he claims targeted the wealthy.

item.title: Kátia Abreu espera conversa com Lula sobre seu papel na eleição do Tocantins
item.description: Kátia Abreu, former Agriculture Minister and senator, announced her affiliation with the PT and said she hopes to speak with Lula to define her role in Tocantins’ elections. She denied plans to run for state governor, saying she is working to build a strong platform to support Lula in the state. Her party switch surprised local politics, given her long history in center-right parties like PP, DEM, and as leader of the agribusiness lobby.

item.title: Jair Bolsonaro deixou um precedente e uma dica eleitoral para Lula
item.description: Lula aims to reduce voter dissatisfaction with the cost of living through fuel subsidies, tax exemptions, and higher taxes on cigarettes and oil exports, with an estimated cost of up to 31 billion reais. He also plans to use presidential authority and public resources to distribute benefits such as income tax exemption for those earning up to R$5,000 monthly, cooking gas for 15 million families, and reduced or zero electricity bills for 60 million families — strategies similar to those employed by Bolsonaro in 2022 to overcome polling deficits.

item.title: A reação nada amigável de ministros do STF a falas de Lula sobre Moraes e o Vorcaro
item.description: Some STF ministers close to Lula expressed dissatisfaction with his criticisms of Alexandre de Moraes' biography and demands for the Court to explain ties between its members and banker Daniel Vorcaro. One justice said Lula's remarks reflect anxiety over his electoral struggles and re-election prospects, calling them unfair and driven by fear of losing the election.

item.title: Divisão no STF sobre RJ antecipa clima de eleições e desenha aliança Kassio-Mendonça
item.description: The STF is divided over whether to hold direct elections for governor of Rio de Janeiro, with ministers Kassio Nunes Marques and André Mendonça opposing the idea that the Supreme Court should review TSE decisions, while Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes, Flávio Dino and Cristiano Zanin support direct elections as an exceptional measure. The lack of consensus led to a request for vista, postponing the decision and keeping Ricardo Couto as acting governor, excluding the PL from power. The conflict reveals tensions between the STF and TSE that foreshadow the political climate of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Como Ricardo Nunes vai colaborar no plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes announced he will contribute to Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential government plan in three areas: urban security, through replicating the Smart Sampa program; food security, via initiatives like Armazém Solidário and community kitchens; and public transportation, by transitioning to an electric bus fleet.

item.title: As reações no STF após tentativa de Lula de se descolar da crise que atinge a Corte
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's attempt to distance himself from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) during the Banco Master crisis provoked an immediate negative reaction from the Court, with his public criticism of Minister Alexandre de Moraes seen as an opportunistic move to shift political blame onto the judiciary. The statement backfired, being interpreted as a sign of fear over losing the election rather than a genuine assertion of independence, further straining the already deteriorating relationship between the Executive and Judicial branches.

item.title: Goleada e denúncia de racismo: Brasil vence a Argentina e garante vaga no Mundial Sub-17
item.description: Brazil defeated Argentina 3-0 in the U-17 South American Championship, securing an early berth for the 2026 World Cup with goals from Riquelme (2) and Eduardo Conceição. However, the match was overshadowed by an alleged racist gesture by an Argentine player toward the Brazilian bench, which the referee failed to act upon under anti-racism protocols, leading to post-match tensions. Despite the incident, Brazil resumed celebrations after technical staff intervened.

item.title: PT aciona o TSE contra vídeos de IA que simulam violência contra mulheres
item.description: The PT filed a representation with the TSE against AI-generated videos simulating violence against its female militants, including physical assaults and hate messages. The party will also send extrajudicial notices to platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook to remove the content.

item.title: Os cachês do governo Lula a influenciadores e artistas
item.description: The Lula government allocated approximately R$ 2 million to digital influencers and artists for advertising campaigns between 2025 and 2026, under the management of Sidônio Palmeira at the Social Communication Secretariat (Secom). The figures were disclosed following a request from the General Controller's Office (CGU) and obtained by Folha via the Access to Information Law. The initiative sparked debate over the use of public funds in institutional communication.

item.title: Datafolha divulga neste sábado pesquisa de intenção de voto para a Presidência
item.description: Datafolha will release on Saturday (11) a new presidential voting intention poll for the 2026 Brazilian election, based on 2,004 interviews with a two-point margin of error. The survey follows the announcement of Ronaldo Caiado as PSD’s pre-candidate and continues a technical tie scenario between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), as seen in prior March and Meio/Ideia polls. This marks the first Datafolha round after Caiado’s entry, maintaining focus on the Lula vs. Bolsonaro showdown.

item.title: Bolsonaro abriu a porta, mas pode ficar de fora
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro opened the door for Brazil’s right by breaking with past stigmas, but his authoritarian style and the figure of Flávio Bolsonaro alienate moderate conservatives. The right in 2026 faces a dilemma: remain hostage to Bolsonarist coup-flirting rhetoric or support candidates who ensure democratic governability — even if that means backing Lula or another non-Bolsonarist figure. Abstention and null votes from a disillusioned right could decide the election in the first round, favoring the continuity of the Lulista project.

item.title: Impeachment de ministros do STF vira prioridade polêmica entre pré-candidatos ao Senado
item.description: Senate pre-candidates are making the impeachment of STF ministers a central campaign banner for 2026, particularly through parties like Novo, which now require explicit commitments from their candidates. Polls show 42.5% of voters view judicial power concentration as the top threat to democracy, surpassing traditional concerns like corruption. Figures such as Marcel van Hattem, Ricardo Salles, and Deltan Dallagnol have already pledged support, signaling a political realignment centered on criticizing the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Polarização entre Lula e Flávio empurra nomes tradicionais do centro para os extremos
item.description: The polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is pushing traditionally centrist politicians toward the extremes, not due to ideological conviction but political survival. Former senator Kátia Abreu, who has switched parties ten times and allied with both left and right governments, recently joined the PT in Tocantins — where centrist candidacies lack space — symbolizing a forced shift to the opposition camp due to the absence of moderate options.

item.title: PT vai ao TSE contra vídeos de IA que simulam agressão a mulheres
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) will file a legal action with the TSE against AI-generated videos simulating assaults on its female militants, depicting them in exorcism-like scenes with slaps and verbal abuse. Communications Secretary Éden Valadares called the content grave, shocking, and inadmissible, stating the move aims to defend the party's image and Brazilian democracy. The videos are circulating on TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram.

item.title: Cármen levou quatro meses para pautar cassação de Cláudio Castro no TSE
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Cármen Lúcia took four months to bring the impeachment process against Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro to the TSE after it was cleared for plenary review. The delay sparked speculation about the case's proceedings, which involve allegations of economic abuse of power and improper use of media during the 2022 election campaign.

item.title: MEC disponibiliza aplicativo gratuito com 8 mil livros
item.description: The MEC launched the free MEC Livros app offering nearly 8,000 literary works in ePub format, featuring Brazilian and international authors, with personalization, gamification, and AI support. President Lula also announced the upcoming MEC Idiomas app, providing 800 self-paced English and Spanish lessons across six levels, enhanced with AI for conversation practice, proficiency testing, and tutoring. The initiative requires an annual investment of R$1.68 million and aims to reach 16,000 students per semester.

item.title: Lula prometeu reabertura do Museu Nacional para 2026, mas a nova previsão é 2029
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva promised in March 2023 the full reopening of the National Museum by the first half of 2026, but the deadline has been postponed to 2029 due to insufficient funding. The renovation, budgeted at R$ 527.7 million, still depends on R$ 164.3 million (31% of the total) to be completed. The 11-year delay since the 2018 fire highlights challenges in managing large-scale cultural projects in Brazil.

item.title: Lula coloca mais 'o pé no chão' e focará em estados de olho nas eleições
item.description: The Lula government is adjusting its 2026 election strategy by prioritizing more informal, grassroots-style events—such as factory, hospital, and local infrastructure visits—where the president moves freely among the public in a 'U'-shaped setup, enhancing perceived closeness and authenticity. This approach leverages Lula’s strength in spontaneous, direct communication, though it raises concerns about potential gaffes. Simultaneously, Secom is developing region-specific materials to showcase local government achievements, directly contrasting them with the Bolsonaro administration’s record.

item.title: Eleições em Hungria, Colômbia e Peru entram no radar do Planalto
item.description: The Brazilian government is monitoring elections in Hungary, Colombia, and Peru as global political indicators, particularly regarding U.S. external influence and international polarization. In Hungary, Viktor Orbán seeks a fifth term against challenger Péter Magyar, with JD Vance’s visit turning the election into a test of U.S. electoral influence. In Latin America, Peru faces a governance crisis while Colombia elects Petro’s successor, both seen as barometers for left and right movements across the continent.

item.title: Por que indicação de Messias demorou quase cinco meses para chegar ao Senado
item.description: The nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF was announced in November 2025 but only formally submitted to the Senate in March 2026 due to resistance from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who preferred Rodrigo Pacheco and stalled the process. The impasse left the STF short one justice for nearly five months, until political pressure and Alcolumbre’s reduced opposition allowed the process to move forward, with the hearing scheduled for April 29.

item.title: Senador sobre colega que rompeu com Lula: “Sempre foi bolsonarista"
item.description: Senator Otto Alencar (PSD-BA) said he was not surprised by his colleague Angelo Coronel’s (Republicanos-BA) decision to support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 elections, stating Coronel has been a bolsonarist since 2019. Their relationship broke down at the end of 2025 after Coronel was excluded from the PT’s 'pure-blood' slate in Bahia and accused the party of greed. Coronel, a former Lula ally, says he will personally vote for Flávio Bolsonaro because the PT did not want him in the state race.

item.title: O "jeito Miriam" de comandar a Casa Civil
item.description: Miriam Belchior, the executive secretary of the Civil House, officially assumed leadership of the ministry on April 2 following Rui Costa’s departure to run for the Senate. Since then, she has adopted a firm profile, holding frequent meetings with ministers and advisors to align key government priorities, as demonstrated by a lunch with Marcelo Costa, Guilherme Boulos, and Sidônio Palmeira at the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Por que Alexandre de Moraes nega-se a falar sobre o Caso Master?
item.description: Alexandre de Moraes, a Supreme Court minister, has avoided commenting on his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master, despite his wife having provided services to the institution. His silence has drawn criticism from supporters who question his impartiality should the case reach the Supreme Court. Experts suggest Moraes may be waiting for the outcome of Vorcaro’s plea deal before addressing potential recusals in the trial.

item.title: ‘Flávio Bolsonaro é uma folha em branco e pode ganhar no 1º turno’, diz marqueteiro de Ratinho Jr.
item.description: Political strategist Jorge Gerez, longtime ally of Ratinho Jr., claims Flávio Bolsonaro is favored to win the 2026 election in the first round, citing 81% of Brazilians wanting change according to Instituto Alfa. He argues that Ratinho Jr.'s withdrawal eliminates space for a third voie, leading to polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, and believes voters prefer a young candidate with a track record — like Flávio — over figures such as Ronaldo Caiado.

item.title: Vice de Flávio Bolsonaro: escolha põe religião no palanque e mede influência eleitoral
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is negotiating with Simone Marquetto (MDB-SP) and Clarissa Tércio (PP-PE) for his 2026 presidential running mate, focusing on religious and regional appeal to boost support among evangelicals and Catholics. Marquetto aims to consolidate the Catholic vote in São Paulo, while Tércio seeks to overcome resistance in the Northeast through her strong evangelical base. The decision will rely on electoral data, as Flávio leads among evangelicals (65.4%) but trails Lula among Catholics (54.2% for the incumbent).

item.title: Aliados históricos apontam fragilidade da Abin e cobram projeto de Lula
item.description: Historical allies of Lula’s government, including José Genoino and Ricardo Berzoini, criticized the weakness of the Abin, citing unclear directives, scarce resources, and the absence of a state intelligence capacity capable of addressing global challenges such as Trumpism and the competition for critical minerals. They urged Lula’s 2026 government program to prioritize intelligence as a strategic asset, blaming foreign influences like the CIA and Mossad for obstructing Abin’s strengthening in Congress.

item.title: Governo Lula não vê risco de Trump atacar urnas na eleição brasileira
item.description: Lula’s aides believe Donald Trump will not challenge the outcome of Brazil’s October elections, as most Brazilians trust the electronic voting system, weakening any U.S. argument against it. They also note that attacks on national sovereignty provoke backlash, particularly among those who value it, which could benefit the left. Despite improved relations, the government remains vigilant about potential U.S. interference, citing the 2025 tariff hike and Magnitsky Act as precedents.

item.title: Golpe, emendas, aborto e inquérito das fake news: os temas que preocupam senadores que vão sabatinar Messias
item.description: The chief minister of the AGU, Jorge Messias, is campaigning to secure the 41 votes needed for his confirmation to the STF, having met personally with nearly all senators. During these meetings, he has heard concerns about the Court’s relationship with Congress, particularly regarding issues such as coup allegations, parliamentary amendments, abortion, and the fake news inquiry.

item.title: Eleições 2026: saiba o caminho das candidaturas até a votação em outubro
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections will take place in two rounds: October 4 (first round) and, if needed, October 25 (second round). Prior to voting, key steps include the party window (March-April), the electoral registration deadline on May 6, party conventions from July 20 to August 5, candidate registration by August 15, and the start of street and online campaigns on August 16. Positions at stake include president, governors, senators, federal, state, and district deputies.

item.title: O que se sabe sobre acordo entre Brasil e EUA para combate ao crime organizado
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced a Brazil-U.S. agreement to strengthen cooperation against transnational organized crime, focusing on intelligence sharing and coordinated actions between Brazil's Federal Revenue and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The Mutual Interdiction Team (MIT) project aims to intercept illegal shipments of weapons and drugs, advancing bilateral cooperation under the Lula and Trump administrations. The announcement comes amid tensions over potential U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations, a politically charged issue in the 2026 election context.

item.title: De apresentador a ex-jogador: partidos lançam famosos atrás de votos
item.description: Brazilian political parties are recruiting celebrities and public figures for the 2026 elections to leverage their popularity as vote-getters. Notable names include former footballer Luís Fabiano (MDB), TV host Val Marchiori (Republicanos), influencer Samuel DPK (MDB), singer Manoel Gomes (Avante), writer Augusto Cury (PSD), and TV host Silvia Abravanel (PSD), all affiliated or pre-candidates for proportional offices, with official candidacies to be confirmed at party conventions in July and August.

item.title: Programa para reduzir dívidas vai funcionar? Especialistas respondem
item.description: The federal government is preparing a package to address record household debt, highlighted by a proposal to release up to R$7 billion from the FGTS severance fund for approximately 10 million workers to pay off debts, potentially serving as a government guarantee to secure lower interest rates in debt refinancing. Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated the measure would apply only to specific debts deemed reasonable for refinancing, as part of a broader strategy to tackle rising family indebtedness (49.7% of income in January 2026) and delinquency, while also examining ways to curb excessive use of sports and electronic betting that could worsen with increased credit access.

item.title: Messias deve ser submetido a arguição rigorosa
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to the CCJ for the STF vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso. The hearing is set for April 29, ruling out rumors of a post-election delay. The vacancy on the Supreme Court is seen as detrimental to the country.

item.title: Três razões para Lula ter jogado Moraes aos leões
item.description: Lula criticized Alexandre de Moraes after revelations about the minister's tripled wealth and ties to Banco Master, stating that public salaries do not allow enrichment during office. The president sought to distance himself from Moraes due to public opinion pressure, as most Brazilians distrust the Supreme Court and view it as allied with his government, harming his electoral prospects. The move also aims to prevent opposition allies like Flávio Bolsonaro from exploiting the scandal against him in 2026.

item.title: Flávio diz a Zema que ex-governador seria um ótimo vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) told Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema (Novo) that Jair Bolsonaro and his base view the former governor as an excellent vice-presidential candidate. The remark was made during a conversation on Friday, April 10, 2026. Zema is being considered as a potential running mate to strengthen the Bolsonarist ticket in the 2026 elections.

item.title: A provocação de Lula a Trump sobre ‘nordestino nervoso’
item.description: Lula made provocative remarks toward Trump, saying the former U.S. president wouldn’t know what a 'nervous northeasterner' is or his alleged descent from Lampião, and that if he did, he wouldn’t threaten Brazil. He emphasized Brazil’s desire for peace and rejection of war, amid global tensions. Despite the joking tone, Lula affirmed cordial relations with Trump and the potential for a White House visit.

item.title: “Quem tem problema não é a direita, é a esquerda”, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, stated that the country's problems come from the left, not the right, during the Liberal Forum at PUCRS. He argued that the multiplicity of conservative names in the electoral race does not represent fragmentation, but a healthy process of diversification.

item.title: Associações indígenas citam temor de 'retorno de um projeto de morte' e declaram apoio à reeleição de Lula
item.description: The Articulation of Indigenous Peoples of Brazil (Apib) and grassroots organizations declared support for Lula's re-election, stating that the 2026 election pits the country against a 'return of a death project' versus democratic continuity. Their support is not blind: they maintain autonomy to demand land demarcation, territorial protection, and strengthened indigenous policies. They condemn Bolsonarism for halting demarcations, inciting violence, and implementing genocidal policies, citing Flávio Bolsonaro as its representative.

item.title: Lula quer incluir estudantes do Fies em novo programa contra dívidas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva proposed including FIES student loan beneficiaries in debt renegotiation programs, citing alarming delinquency that reached R$17.9 billion in 2025, with 59.3% of beneficiaries in arrears. He argued that educating these students yields long-term productive returns for the country and that the government cannot 'take away the dream' of those financing higher education. FIES, which funds low-income students in private colleges, has active contracts totaling R$93.8 billion, with an average delinquency of R$46,000 per student.

item.title: Flávio condiciona escolha de senadores favoráveis a “impeachment de ministros”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for President of Brazil, stated that the selection of senators should consider their stance on the impeachment of ministers of the Federal Supreme Court (STF). Speaking at the Liberty Forum in Porto Alegre, he emphasized this as a key factor in choosing Senate allies.

item.title: Por que o entorno de Lula acompanha ‘com lupa’ escândalo que chegou ao STF
item.description: The plea bargain of businessman Maurício Camisotti reveals a national fraud scheme in the INSS, involving the unauthorized deduction of billions from retirees’ benefits, money laundering through law firms, and the participation of INSS servers, union entities, political operators, and legislators. Lula’s inner circle is monitoring the case closely due to fears it could reach figures near the government, including possible links to the president’s son, and its potential to destabilize the political landscape ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Se Trump soubesse o que é um nordestino nervoso, não brigaria com o Brasil, diz Lula
item.description: During a visit to the IFSP in Sorocaba (SP), Lula joked that Donald Trump would not provoke Brazil if he knew what a 'nervous northeasterner' is, referencing his lineage from Lampião. He reiterated Brazil’s desire for peace and non-involvement in international conflicts, such as the U.S.-Iran tensions, stating that those who seek war should go to 'the other side of the world'.

item.title: Beto Preto inaugura obras com Ratinho Jr em vários municípios ao longo da semana
item.description: Federal deputy Beto Preto accompanied Governor Ratinho Jr in a week-long agenda of infrastructure project inaugurations across several municipalities in Paraná, reinforcing his commitment to municipalism and regional development.

item.title: “Trump não sabe o que é um nordestino nervoso”, ameaça Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized Donald Trump for not understanding Northeastern Brazilian culture, stating that the former U.S. president would not dare threaten Brazil if he knew what a 'nervous Northeasterner' is like. The comment was made during the inauguration of a campus of the Federal Institute of São Paulo on Friday morning, the 10th.

item.title: Lula admite que precisa de um psicólogo durante evento no ABC
item.description: During an event in the ABC region, President Lula responded to a woman interested in studying Psychology, encouraging her to pursue the degree and saying she could 'take care of him'. The remark was interpreted as an informal acknowledgment that he may need psychological support.

item.title: Fachin diz que Corte chancelou Ricardo Couto no governo do RJ
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Justice Edson Fachin stated that the Court has endorsed the continued interim governance of Rio de Janeiro by Justice Ricardo Couto while awaiting the TSE's ruling on Cláudio Castro's conviction. The remarks were made during a Human Rights Observatory meeting at the TJ-RJ, emphasizing judicial support for the temporary arrangement. Couto has held the Guanabara Palace since March 24, 2026, following Castro's resignation and the departure of his vice, Thiago Pampolha.
